newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Wednesday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange but off highs due to poor sentiment, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 19,700 yuan ($2,373) per tonne, rising 100 yuan. It opened at 19,800, hitting an intra-day high of 19,850 and a low of 19,680.
October fell 40 to 19,860 yuan, November rose 90 to 19,750, December dropped 10 to 19,620, February increased 100 to 19,700, March 80 to 19,720 and April 50 to 19,800.
Combined volume fell to 45,280 tonnes from 64,510.
Copper opened up sharply on overnight gains on the LME but long liquidation and fresh selling at high levels on poor sentiment pushed the prices steadily down for most of the session.

"Later-maturing contracts met strong resistance today at the 19,800 yuan level because many investors were still pessimistic about the market trend," one trader said. "Today's rise may be only a normal correction after Tuesday's falls."
Traders said weak domestic spot demand made some producers sell copper in the futures markets and Shanghai copper had little interest in keeping up with LME rises.
"Long position holders had no confidence in holding copper above 20,000 yuan because of poor fundamentals," a second trader said.
Analysts said it would be hard for copper to move back above the 20,000 yuan resistance level which was breached on Tuesday until LME copper rises above $2,000.
Aluminium ended mixed. October fell 40 to 13,860 yuan per tonne and November rose 50 to 13,700.
Combined volume fell to 1,140 tonnes from 1,650.
